title: values_proven v1 - the compiled currency
description: The compiled answer to a contract's `required_values[]`: one row per value id the candidate claims to have proven, and the evidence backing the claim. Rows are STATION CLAIMS, not a verifier's own findings - a downstream verifier checks that the claim exists, names a station, carries evidence, and that any subject_digest it cites is genuinely one of this entry's images. It cannot re-run a station. THIS FILE IS THE ADDRESSABLE DEFINITION; `channel-entry.schema.json` embeds the same shape inline, because that is the copy the in-cluster verifier enforces against a signed entry. The two are held identical by `publisher/tests/test_value_chain.py::EmbeddedValuesProven`, which resolves the embedded $refs and compares - a drift between them is a finding, not a variant.

id.description: The contract's `required_values[].id` this row answers (e.g. V-est-1). Matched by exact string, so a typo is a missing proof, not a silent pass.

verdict.description: `proven` - a station ran something and the evidence rows say what. `waived` - a NAMED HUMAN accepted the value unproven for this entry; `waived_by` is then mandatory, because an anonymous waiver is indistinguishable from an omission.

evidence.description: What was actually done. Mandatory and non-empty on a `proven` row: a proven verdict with no evidence is the exact shape of the void this block exists to close.

what.description: The finding, in the words the station recorded it in - verbatim from the station's own fill line where the row came from a fills log.

ref.description: Where that finding is committed and can be re-read: a path in the stations ledger, a URL, a receipt id.

subject_digest.description: The image this evidence was produced against, when the evidence is image-specific. The verifier requires it to appear in this entry's `images[].index_digest` set - evidence collected against a digest this entry does not ship proves nothing about this entry.

station.description: Which station made the claim. An unattributable proof is worse than none, for the same reason an unattributable verdict is.

waived_by.description: The human who accepted the value unproven. Required on a `waived` row and meaningless on a `proven` one.
